intro: Driving verbs, road signs, breakdowns, fines and insurance.
b1.titulo: Everything a driver needs to say
b1.texto:
**The verbs.** **Arrancar** el coche, **acelerar**, **frenar**, **girar**, **adelantar**, **aparcar**, **dar marcha atrás**. **Poner el intermitente.** **Tocar el claxon.** **Ponerse el cinturón.** **Reducir la velocidad.**

**The roads.** **Una autopista** (often **de peaje**), **una autovía** (free), **una carretera nacional**, **una carretera comarcal**. On them: **una curva**, **un cruce**, **una rotonda**, **un bache** (pothole), **un área de descanso**.

**The signs.** **Ceda el paso.** **Stop.** **Prohibido aparcar.** **Dirección prohibida.** **Dirección obligatoria.** **Curva peligrosa.** **Zona azul** is paid street parking.

**The papers.** **El carné de conducir**, which you **te sacas** and later **renuevas**; in Spain it is **un carné por puntos**, and offences take points away. **El permiso de circulación**, **el seguro**, **la matrícula**.

**When it goes wrong.** **Tener un pinchazo.** **Quedarse sin gasolina.** **Perder el control.** **Salirse de la carretera.** **Darse un golpe.** **Chocar contra** un árbol. Then **la grúa** takes the car to **el taller**, where they do **una reparación** or **una revisión**.

**The law.** **Me han puesto una multa por** exceso de velocidad. **Me han quitado tres puntos.**

**Insurance.** **Contratar un seguro** **a todo riesgo** (comprehensive) or **a terceros** (third party). After an accident, the company pays **una indemnización**.

**On foot.** **El peatón** crosses at **el paso de cebra**.
b2.titulo: A bad day on the road
b2.f0: I left home in good time, but the car would not start and I lost twenty minutes before I managed it.
b2.f1: To make them up I took the toll motorway instead of the dual carriageway.
b2.f2: I was overtaking a lorry when I noticed the steering wheel shaking: I had a puncture.
b2.f3: I put the indicator on, braked little by little and stopped at a rest area.
b2.f4: As the spare wheel was flat too, I had to call the insurance company so that they would send a tow truck.
b2.f5: While I was waiting, an officer came up and fined me for not wearing the reflective vest.
b2.f6: I got to the garage at two and to the meeting, of course, I never got at all.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, why was the driver fined?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Por no llevar el chaleco reflectante.
b4.o1.refuerzo: Speeding is a distractor; the question asks for the reason the text gives for the fine.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, why couldn't he change the wheel himself?
b5.o0.refuerzo: La rueda de repuesto también estaba desinflada.
b6.pregunta: Which sign tells you to let other cars go first?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Ceda el paso means give way: the sign telling drivers to let others go first.
b7.pregunta: Complete: he crashed into a tree.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Chocar contra means to crash into, so contra is the right preposition.
b7.o1.refuerzo: The preposition is contra, or con.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The preposition is contra, or con.
b8.o0.refuerzo: Poner el intermitente means to indicate: switch on the turn signal before turning.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That is to sound the horn.
b9.o0: I've had two points taken off my licence.
b9.o1: They have left me two points on my licence.
b9.o2: I've been given two points for my card.
b10.traduccion: The car wouldn't start and I had to call the tow truck.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write an accident report for your insurance company: where, when, how it happened and the damage.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Give your opinion aloud on speed limits, the points-based licence or cars in city centres.
b9.o0.explicacion: Me han quitado dos puntos del carné means two points were taken off my licence.
